notes: **Basidiocarp.** The mushroom is the fleshy fruiting body of a basidiomycete, with a cap (pileus), stalk (stipe) and gills (lamellae) on which basidiospores are produced.
**Edible mushrooms.** Agaricus bisporus (button mushroom) and Pleurotus (oyster mushroom) are cultivated widely and are rich in protein, vitamins and minerals.
**Poisonous mushrooms.** Amanita muscaria (fly agaric) and other toxic species contain deadly toxins; misidentification can cause severe poisoning, so wild mushrooms must never be eaten unverified.
**Ecological role.** Many mushrooms are decomposers, and forest trees depend on mycorrhizal fungal associations for mineral and water absorption.
**Cultivation.** Mushroom farming uses composted substrate spawned with fungal mycelium under humid, shaded conditions — a growing cottage industry in Nepal.
